statement: The revived Rubin CPX is reported to carry 168 GB of HBM4, replacing the 128 GB of GDDR7 in the earlier CPX design.
why: Swapping commodity graphics memory for HBM on a high-volume inference part pulls yet more scarce HBM into NVIDIA's bill of materials.

impact.mechanism: Moving a SKU from GDDR7 to HBM4 raises HBM content per shipped accelerator, tightening an already constrained memory supply if the reported specification holds.

evidence.source: Investing.com (citing TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo)
evidence.excerpt: 168 GB of HBM4, compared to 288 GB on Rubin and 128 GB of GDDR7 in the earlier CPX version.

reasoning: The memory change is described in an analyst note about an unreleased 2027 part; volumes are unknown, so the supply effect is a directional inference, not a measured draw on HBM bits.

confidence.basis: Unconfirmed specification for an unreleased product from a single analyst note; no unit volumes stated.
